detailed_rationale: Swiggy is India's #2 food-delivery platform and #2/#3 quick-commerce player (Instamart), plus a smaller Out-of-Home (events/ticketing) business and a 'supply chain and distribution' segment. [DATA] FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to Rs 23,053cr (from Rs 15,227cr in FY25), but consolidated net loss WIDENED to Rs 4,154cr from Rs 3,117cr in FY25. Segment revenue split FY26: supply-chain & distribution Rs 10,935cr (largest single line - this reflects Instamart's owned-inventory retail sales booked gross, not pure platform commission, so headline revenue growth overstates platform-economics growth relative to GOV growth [INFERENCE, standard for owned-inventory quick-commerce accounting, not line-item-verified against the shareholder letter]), food delivery Rs 7,832cr, quick-commerce platform Rs 3,859cr. Food delivery GOV grew 22.6% YoY to Rs 9,005cr in Q4 FY26 alone (a 15-quarter high), with quarterly adjusted EBITDA +39.8% YoY to Rs 297cr and FULL-YEAR adjusted EBITDA crossing Rs 1,000cr for the first time - the core business is now a genuine, if modest, self-funding line. Instamart GOV grew 68.8% YoY to Rs 7,881cr in Q4 FY26 but contribution margin remains -1.8% of GOV (improved 65bps QoQ) and the segment posted an EBITDA loss of Rs 858cr in the quarter alone; dark-store count reached 1,143 stores / 129 cities / 4.8mn sq ft. [DATA] Q4 FY26 (quarter ended Mar-2026, reported 8-May-2026) is the latest HARD print: consolidated revenue Rs 6,383cr (+45% YoY), net loss narrowed YoY to Rs 800cr from Rs 1,081cr. Q1 FY27 (quarter ended Jun-2026) has NOT yet been reported - earnings call is scheduled 30-Jul-2026 - so this is a catalyst-AHEAD quarter as of this note (21-Jul-2026). [DATA, Q4 FY26 concall, 8-May-2026] On earnings quality: no major one-off gains/credits identified in the searched releases; the growth-vs-loss split looks like genuine operating economics rather than an accounting artifact. But management's own GUIDANCE moved adversely on the same call - Instamart contribution-margin breakeven is still guided for the Jun-2026 quarter, but the previously-guided absolute EBITDA-breakeven timeline for quick commerce was pushed OUT a full year, from ~FY28E to FY29E, with management citing 'uncertainty about market structure and intense competition' and declining to commit to a firmer date. That is a genuine negative revision, not conservative sandbagging. [DATA/third-party estimate, not independently verified methodology] On competitive structure: Blinkit (Eternal) leads Indian quick commerce with ~46% share vs Instamart's ~24% and Zepto's ~22% per one mid-2026 industry tracker (Datum Intelligence); Blinkit is already adjusted-EBITDA-profitable and outspends peers, structurally capping Instamart's ability to raise take-rates while still chasing share. In food delivery, Rapido entered with a zero-commission 'Ownly' brand in Mar-2026, prompting Swiggy to run its own discount sub-brand 'Toing' (launched Sep-2025); early read (JPMorgan, mid-2026) is Toing holding share better than Ownly so far, but the need for a discount sub-brand at all signals renewed take-rate pressure in what had been a stabilizing food-delivery market. Swiggy exited its 12% Rapido stake for Rs 2,400cr shortly after Ownly's launch - sensible capital discipline, but it also removes Swiggy's hedge against that new entrant.
recommendation_rationale: Quant final_score is 39/39 (1y and 3y) -> Sell, driven by a very poor quality_score (5.4, reflecting ROE -26.6% / ROCE -27.1% - the whole company still consumes capital) despite high growth scores (91-93) and a moderate value_score (72); bs_flag is RED. My own research agrees with, rather than overrides, that Sell: growth is real (both GOV lines show genuine momentum and food delivery is now solidly EBITDA-positive), but the segment doing the damage (Instamart) just had its own EBITDA-breakeven timeline pushed a full year further out by management, competitive intensity is rising on BOTH fronts (a scaled, profitable Blinkit in quick commerce; a zero-commission new entrant in food delivery), and the stock's sharp de-rating from post-listing highs (~Rs474 52-week high to ~Rs277 now) shows the market pricing the burn, not ignoring the good news. I see no specific, falsifiable reason to invoke the Sell->Hold rescue here - the bear case is intact and got incrementally worse this quarter (the FY28->FY29 EBITDA-breakeven push-out), so I am keeping Sell.
summary: Swiggy's food-delivery business has become a real, if modest, profit generator, but the company overall keeps losing MORE money each year (Rs 4,154cr FY26 loss, up from Rs 3,117cr) because its Instamart quick-commerce arm is still burning cash chasing growth against a bigger, already-profitable rival (Blinkit) and a new low-cost entrant in food delivery (Rapido's Ownly). Management itself just pushed back its own timeline for quick-commerce to reach full profitability by an extra year. Until that burn visibly narrows, we rate this a Sell.
positive_para: Revenue is compounding fast and broadly - FY26 revenue +51% YoY to Rs 23,053cr across three large-TAM businesses. Food delivery just posted its best GOV growth in 15 quarters (+22.6% YoY) while turning solidly EBITDA-positive (over Rs 1,000cr for the full year), proving the core platform can fund itself. Instamart's contribution margin has improved 65bps sequentially to -1.8% and management still guides to contribution-margin breakeven in the Jun-2026 quarter, with the Out-of-Home segment fully profitable for the first time in FY26. The stock has also de-rated substantially from its post-IPO peak (Rs474 to ~Rs277), which limits, though does not eliminate, further multiple-compression risk if execution stays on track.
negative_para: The company is losing MORE money every year, not less: FY26's Rs 4,154cr net loss is wider than FY25's Rs 3,117cr, and the segment responsible (quick commerce) just had its own EBITDA-breakeven target pushed a full year further out (FY28->FY29) by management on the Q4 FY26 call, citing competitive uncertainty - the single most important data point here, since even the company's own operators lack visibility into when the burn stops. On top of that, Instamart trails a scaled, already-profitable Blinkit by roughly half its market share, meaning Swiggy cannot outspend its way to leadership without extending losses further; and food delivery - the one profitable leg - now faces a zero-commission new entrant (Rapido's Ownly) that has already forced Swiggy into its own discount sub-brand (Toing), reintroducing take-rate pressure just as that segment was stabilizing. Negative ROE (-26.6%) and ROCE (-27.1%) confirm the whole business remains a net consumer, not generator, of capital, with no credible sub-3-year line of sight to consolidated profitability.
reverse_dcf_judgment: PE is negative (loss-making), so Price/Sales is the workable lens: ~2.67x trailing sales on a ~Rs71-75k cr market cap against ~Rs23-27k cr TTM revenue. Paying ~2.7x sales for a business where two of three segments are still EBITDA-negative, and whose largest-growth segment just had its own breakeven timeline extended, implicitly underwrites several more years of 30%+ topline growth PLUS a credible path to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margins thereafter - a path management itself would not commit a date to. The multiple has already compressed a great deal from listing (market cap crossed Rs1 lakh crore near IPO vs ~Rs71-75k crore now) but not enough, in my view, to fully price in an extra year of quick-commerce cash burn against an already-profitable, scaled leader (Blinkit). Verdict: fair-to-rich, not cheap - not a screaming short at this multiple, but not cheap enough to justify a Sell->Hold rescue either. [INFERENCE - my own multiple framework, not a formal DCF model]
